description: Recorded payment cannot override denied authority.
Ambiguous payment holds only after protected gates pass.
Payment is requested only when every protected gate passes.
Refusal remains blocking even with a satisfied payment condition.
Changing only payment cannot change a refusal decision.
Withheld participation is unresolved rather than inferred as acceptance.
Addition above JavaScript safe integer range remains exact.
Amounts with distinct unit identities cannot be combined.
A JSON number is not a wire amount.
Canonical decimal strings reject leading zeroes.
Wire amounts reject values above unsigned 256-bit magnitude.
An unexpired admission cannot begin execution if it is not the trusted gate head.
Only a newly committed BEGIN transition emits one namespaced effect intent.
A serialized APPLIED projection cannot unlock an effect without its exact ledger entry.
An effect that may have run is reconciled rather than stranded by later refusal.
Posting unit and ledger domain must match the registered account.
Each quoted asset leg balances independently.
Numerically equal deficits in different units cannot cancel.
Append validates reversal invariants already present in the supplied journal.
An exact repeated ledger key replays without a second entry.
Split postings may sum to exactly the per-unit uint256 boundary.
Individually valid postings cannot overflow a per-unit uint256 total.
Ambiguous submission recovery reconciles and never automatically retries.
Ledger-first recovery replays one fixed application entry and finalizes payment once after unrelated ledger progress.
A different transaction cannot occupy the fixed application idempotency key.
An applied payment projection without its exact application ledger entry fails closed.
A different transaction cannot occupy the fixed application request fingerprint.
A finalized application ledger time must equal its derived payment transition time.
The derived application transition ID cannot be consumed by an earlier operation.
A composed application rejects a ledger that already occupies a future fixed reversal identity.
One payment key cannot identify two different content-derived quotes.
A ledger-first application cannot claim a time before external settlement was observed.
Fixed application and reversal entries cannot bypass their derived payment transitions.
A stale ledger-first application after external reversal is compensated exactly and replays after a later entry.
Orphaned application compensation cannot predate the observed external reversal.
Account and payment registries must agree on the exact definition behind each unit ID.
Ledger-first recovery replays one fixed applied-path reversal and finalizes payment after unrelated ledger progress.
A generic reversal cannot reverse the fixed payment reversal and reactivate value.
An applied-path reversed projection without its exact compensating ledger entry fails closed.
An applied-path reversal ledger time must equal its derived payment transition time.
The derived applied-reversal transition ID cannot encode an external pre-application reversal.
A balanced but underpaid ledger transaction cannot apply a larger quote.
The same price identity cannot name a different ratio in another call.
Pinned rational conversion remains exact above JS safe integer range.
An inexact remainder result exposes no spendable truncated output.
One price book rejects overlapping 1000 and 10000 input rates.
Half-open price intervals select the successor at the exact boundary.
Semantic quote identity is independent of input object insertion order.
A quote identity cannot be reused for changed exact amount terms.
A payment quote cannot encode a zero-value exchange that has no reachable ledger application.
Top-level collection accessors are rejected without invoking their getter.
An own __proto__ field cannot disappear during snapshot validation.
Wallet credit and project API credit remain distinct despite a shared display word.
